conviction_note: The findings net to zero: the Nov 5 satellite reorder arrived 'sooner than anticipated' and should let management firm the back-half-weighted FY27 guide (+0.7), but the stock has already run +17% in 20 days on it. Against that, simple arithmetic on the 10-K's 41% customer concentration puts Q1 revenue near $7.3-7.8M, a little under the single-analyst $7.9M (-0.5), and gross margin loses the satellite mix plus about 3 points of one-off tariff refunds (-0.2, inside guidance). So p_up is 51 on an abs move of 7 (thin $100k/day name, guidance commentary likely), giving +0.14.
bar: Q1 FY27 (Sept quarter) revenue $7.9M and EPS -$0.07 come from one analyst (Lucid Capital Markets, Buy, $8 target, initiated 2026-05-18; https://www.investing.com/equities/precision-optics-consensus-estimates). The revenue figure is from Benzinga's estimates page as relayed by search (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/POCI/earnings-forecasts, 403 on fetch, snippet_only), and the EPS figure is also shown on Yahoo per the same snippet. The bar therefore has one source and is capped. The company gave no numeric Q1 guide: satellite-customer revenue down ~40% sequentially in Q1 and lower again in Q2; FY27 revenue $30-33M and adj. EBITDA -$1.2M to -$1.7M (https://finviz.com/news/396164/precision-optics-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2026-financial-results, 2026-09-28).
positioning_check: Short interest ~11K shares, 0.1% of float, 1.0 days to cover as of 2026-09-11 (https://equibles.com/stocks/poci/shortinterest); MarketBeat 0.3 days in late May 2026. Not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism. No options market (baseline options.status no_options_market), so no skew. Tape: spot $5.00 intraday 2026-11-16 (-4.4% on the day), run_up_20d +17.1% from $4.23 (10-22) to $5.23 (11-13), 16% below the 52w high. 20-day average volume is ~20.5K shares, about $100k/day.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-05 POCI announced a $2M follow-on production order from its existing top-tier aerospace satellite customer, the 41%-of-FY26-revenue customer whose pause drove the guided ~40% Q1 cut. The CEO said the order came 'sooner than anticipated', with shipments starting December and running 2-3 months. That supports a firmed (or less back-end-dependent) FY27 guide of $30-33M and a smaller Q2 trough than the 'further decline in Q2' guided on 2026-09-28.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When the satellite pause was guided on the 2026-09-28 print, the stock went $4.63 to $4.15 over three sessions (-10%) on 5-10x volume. When the FY26 guide was raised and beaten on the May 2026 print (05-13 amc), it gained +3.9% the next day and +10% within four sessions. On the Nov 5 order day itself it rose +2.3% ($4.84 to $4.95).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced as a fact: the stock is +17% from its 10-22 low. What is not priced is how management translates it into the Q2 and Q3 shape and the FY27 range on tonight's call. A priced firm-up would show the stock above its pre-pause level (~$4.6-4.8 late September) plus a premium; at $5.00 it is only modestly above it, and the one-analyst coverage leaves no preview carrying an updated Q2 number.
findings.independence: Same customer story as the 2026-09-28 call transcript, where the CEO said 'the most recent communications indicate a recovery by the end of fiscal 2027' (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262191776-tradingkey). That source is the company too. No independent counterparty series for the unnamed satellite customer was found.

findings.finding: Q1 revenue arithmetic: the FY26 10-K says one customer was 41% of FY26 revenue (~$12.9M of $31.5M), consistent with the ~$12-13M satellite run rate. A 40% sequential cut from Q4's ~$3.1M is ~-$1.25M. With the rest flat at Q4's ~$5.65M (Ross +55% y/y, the $3.5M ophthalmic follow-on ramping, the $1.3M defense follow-on), Q1 revenue lands near $7.3-7.8M against the single-analyst $7.9M bar. Year on year that is still above Q1 FY26's $6.68M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is only one baseline history move (-5.74% as tagged, -2.16% if bmo, 2026-09-28), and that print turned on the forward cut rather than the record Q4. In May 2026 a revenue beat with a raised guide bought +3.9% the next day.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar is one analyst's model, and the gap is within that model's noise. If the market had fully priced a sub-$7.9M print, the stock would not have rallied 17% into it. It lands inside what the company guided (a ~40% satellite cut), so it is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect, capped small.
findings.independence: Q4 revenue of $8.77M and the satellite cut come from the 2026-09-28 release and call (https://finviz.com/news/396164/precision-optics-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2026-financial-results; https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262191776-tradingkey), a different document from the 10-K concentration figure but the same company. The non-satellite offset (ophthalmic ramp, defense follow-on) cuts the other way and is netted in the size.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26 gross margin of 25.3% included about 3 points from non-recurring IEEPA tariff refunds (FY26 was 17.2%, and Q1 FY26 was 14.2%). The satellite program carries higher margins than the revenue replacing it, so Q1 margin should step down toward the high teens, and management already guided a return to quarterly losses early in FY27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY26 EBITDA guide of +$0.5M became -$2.1M while revenue beat by ~$6M, and the stock still rose on the May print. This holder base has looked through margin when revenue and the outlook held.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The company guided losses early in the year and an adj. EBITDA loss of $1.2-1.7M for FY27, and the -$0.07 EPS bar (~-$0.77M net loss) already embeds a step-down. Only a margin below ~15% would surprise.
findings.independence: Q1 FY26 margin of 14.2% at $6.68M revenue (https://www.streetinsider.com/Press+Releases/Precision+Optics+Reports+First+Quarter+Fiscal+Year+2026+Financial+Results/25607698.html, 2025-11-13) shows how margin behaves at sub-$7M quarters. That is a different document.

findings.finding: The balance sheet does not force financing: cash was $9.84M and bank debt ~$1.29M at 2026-06-30, FY26 operating cash burn was $1.55M, and the CEO said there are no plans to raise equity in FY27 'unless we have some unusual events'. The only share registration since is a routine S-8 (2026-10-30) for 540K equity-plan shares (~4.9%). The 10-30 8-K item 1.01 is only a one-year renewal of the Gardner, MA facility lease.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The company raised equity in March 2026 ($10.6M net) and in FY25 (registered direct). No print-day financing has been recorded in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing to price. It is filed so the panel can see the financing trail the sweep asked about came back clean. A Q1 burn of ~$1-1.5M leaves ~$8.5M, with no going-concern language in the 10-K.
findings.independence: Cash and the no-raise statement come from the 2026-09-28 release and call (https://finviz.com/news/396164/precision-optics-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2026-financial-results; https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262191776-tradingkey).

outside_window.finding: A second satellite-constellation customer placed two ~$50K engineering orders and targets production in 6-12 months, which per management could affect only late FY27 (Q4, June 2027). This is upside to the guide that the window cannot see unless it is quantified on the call.
Annual meeting on 2026-12-10, a routine slate (directors, say-on-pay, auditor) with no authorized-share increase.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR submissions since 2026-09-28: only Form 4 grants (CFO shares in lieu of cash at the $4.427 VWAP, code A, not an open-market buy), DEF 14A, S-8 and the lease 8-K; no 8-K pre-announcement, no item 2.02 before tonight, no 424B or ATM
Independent series for the unnamed satellite customer: none found that would confirm the timing of a demand recovery outside the company's own releases
Analyst previews: one analyst (Lucid Capital, Buy, $8); no fresh preview or estimate change found
Older order headlines (the $723K AR order dated 2025-11-07, the $1.3M urology development order dated 2023-04-19) were checked and are stale, not new information

rejected_candidates.candidate: Run-up of +17% in 20 days into a print guided weak, as a sell-the-news positioning negative
rejected_candidates.detail: The run-up is the market pricing the 2026-11-05 satellite reorder (finding 1), so it is netted into that finding's size rather than counted as a separate negative.

rejected_candidates.candidate: StockAlarm shows an FY27 revenue average of $35M, above the company's $30-33M guide
rejected_candidates.detail: Single-aggregator figure, inconsistent with the company guide in the 2026-09-28 release and the one-analyst coverage; not used as the bar.

baseline_tension: No skew exists. The +17% run-up agrees with the positive guidance finding, so that finding is largely priced, while the slight Q1 revenue shortfall against one analyst cuts against the run-up. Net is balanced, and p_up sits at 51.
lessons_applied: Lesson 3/read-the-set: the draft's separate -0.5 run-up positioning finding was the market pricing the same Nov 5 order, so it was merged into the order finding, which went from +1.0 to +0.7 net, and the positioning item moved to rejected_candidates as a duplicate.
Lesson 6: the bar has one analyst and one fetchable source, so the Q1 revenue finding stays capped at -0.5, and the margin finding lands inside guided losses and moves toward 0 (-0.3 to -0.2).
Lesson 8: thin coverage and ~$100k/day turnover keep abs_move_pct at 7.0, above the single baseline reaction of 5.74; p_up moved from 52 to 51 because the remaining findings net to zero.
Lesson 4: financing was checked (cash $9.8M, no raise planned, S-8 routine) and kept at 0.0.
